01 / ME

Diego
Pérez Obrero.

Graphic designer and software developer for film and TV shows.

I bring a wide range of artistic and digital tools to the graphic challenges of filmmaking. Specialising in graphic props for film and television, I combine creativity, technical skill and an eye for detail to bring a production’s visual world to life. My degree in Fine Arts gives each project a strong aesthetic and conceptual foundation.

A Facebook scholarship took me to an intensive six-month bootcamp at DEV/f in Mexico City, where I trained in HTML, CSS, JavaScript and React. These skills allow me to integrate digital tools into my creative practice and solve the challenges of screens and new technologies on set.

  • Degree in Fine Arts — Universidad de Sevilla
  • Facebook Developers Scholarship — DEV/f, Mexico City
  • C1 Advanced in English — University of Cambridge
GRAPHIC PROPSSOFTWARE DEVELOPMENTFILM / TV
02 / MY WORKING TOOLS

A tool for
every idea.

From visual identity
to on-set playback.

My work brings together graphic design, custom typography and software development to shape the visual identity of a production. With a strong command of the Adobe suite, I create digital illustrations, print-ready artwork, set sketches, posters and pitch decks that help define and communicate its look. Custom typefaces developed in FontLab give that identity a distinctive voice, down to the smallest letter.

That same attention to detail carries through to the screen. Using HTML, CSS and JavaScript, alongside React and GSAP, I build and animate interactive interfaces and digital props tailored to the needs of each scene.

On set, I bring this content into the action as a playback operator. Working with Resolume, I cue and control video and motion graphics, coordinating their timing with the performance and the crew to support each take.

ADOBEHTML / CSS / JAVASCRIPTREACT / GSAPPLAYBACK / RESOLUME

My working tools: Photoshop, Illustrator, InDesign, After Effects, Resolume, JavaScript, HTML, CSS, React, GSAP, Figma, Proto.io, ProtoPie and FontLab.

03 / CRAFT AND MATERIAL

The mark
of the hand.

An artistic foundation.
A hands-on approach.

My training in Fine Arts shapes the way I approach a production, from the first visual ideas to the finished pieces on set. I create set sketches, concept art and storyboards to explore spaces, establish a visual language and help communicate how a scene will unfold.

That process continues through artistic painting for sets, hand lettering and bespoke graphic props. Working directly with paint, paper and other materials lets me give each piece its own character and a sense of belonging to the world of the story.

Whenever the production schedule allows, I like to make props using the same methods that would have been used to create their real-world counterparts. Following the original process brings authentic textures, marks and small imperfections that make an object feel genuine.

FINE ARTSCONCEPT ART / STORYBOARDSPAINTING / GRAPHIC PROPS
04 / SCREENS AND CODE

Stories
become interactive.

Digital props & fake user interfaces (FUI) for film and television.

I design fictional apps, interactive screens and motion graphics that belong to the story, and work as a Lead Standby Motion Graphics operator on set.

Since 2018, I have been developing websites alongside my work in film. Combining graphic design with HTML, CSS, JavaScript and React, I create digital experiences that bring a visual idea to life and respond to the person using them.

On set, that interaction makes a difference: a screen that responds to an actor's actions helps them stay immersed in the scene, with natural timing and something tangible to react to. Capturing those responses in camera can also reduce the need for screen replacements in post-production and save substantial VFX costs.

Make sure to check out my Digital Props section if you haven't already.

05 / ROOTED HERE, CONNECTED EVERYWHERE

From Seville,
with love.

Local knowledge. International perspective.

Based between Seville and Madrid, I bring an extensive network of printers, prop makers and specialist film suppliers to every production. Knowing who to call helps me find the right materials, coordinate fabrication and turn ideas into finished pieces within the realities of a shooting schedule.

I am available to work on location or remotely, anywhere in the world. Whether joining an art department on set or collaborating across time zones, I adapt to the way each team works and keep communication clear throughout the process.

Having lived in England and worked on international productions, I am fluent in English and comfortable using it in the day-to-day rhythm of a film crew. My Cambridge C1 Advanced qualification supports that experience, allowing me to discuss creative briefs, resolve technical details and collaborate confidently with teams from around the world.
